description: Count a federal civil deadline the way Fed. R. Civ. P. 6 counts it. Send the trigger date (the event: service, entry of judgment, a hearing date), the number of days, and whether the period runs after or before the event. The trigger day is left out, every day is counted, and a last day on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday moves to the next day that is not one (backward for periods before an event). Federal legal holidays are built in on the days they are observed; send state holidays, days declared holidays by the President or Congress, and days the clerk's office was inaccessible as lists. If the time runs after being served by mail, by leaving it with the clerk, or by other means consented to, 3 days are added under Rule 6(d). Get back the deadline, every day skipped and why, when the last day ends, and, for a period after an event, an earlier date to file by when the deadline moved past a holiday observed on another day than its date. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/frcp-deadline). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

clerk_inaccessible.description: Days the clerk's office was inaccessible (weather, a filing-system outage), YYYY-MM-DD (up to 40). A filing deadline on such a day moves to the next accessible day (Rule 6(a)(3)). Periods after an event only.

days.description: The period in days, as the rule, order or statute states it (14, 21, 28, 30, 90 ...).

declared_holidays.description: Other days declared a holiday by the President or Congress (an Executive order closing federal offices, a national day of mourning), YYYY-MM-DD (up to 40). Counted both ways (Rule 6(a)(6)(B)).

direction.description: after (default): act within N days after the event. before: act at least N days before the event (the trigger_date is then the event, such as a hearing).

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'answer to complaint' (your own text, echoed; not a party name).

served_by.description: Only when the time runs after being served: how the paper was served under Rule 5(b)(2). mail, left_with_clerk and other_consented add 3 days (Rule 6(d)); electronic and in_person (handed over or left at the office or home) add none.

state_holidays.description: Holidays declared by the state where the district court sits, YYYY-MM-DD (up to 40). Counted only for periods after an event (Rule 6(a)(6)(C)).

trigger_date.description: Date of the event that starts the count (service, entry of the order, the hearing), YYYY-MM-DD. From 2016-12-01.
